oneLine: Organist, harpsichordist, conductor, composer, and writer, working at the intersection of the pipe organ, the Catholic liturgy, and the sacred music of Latin America.
short: Dr. Adán Alejándro Fernández is Director of Music and Liturgy and Organist at Holy Family Catholic Church in Glendale, California, and University Organist and piano faculty at California Lutheran University. He is a harpsichordist with the early music consort Hortus Musicus, teaches music theory at the Colburn School, and founded the Glendale Youth Symphony. He holds a Doctor of Musical Arts in sacred music from the University of Southern California.
long: Dr. Adán Alejándro Fernández is a versatile musician and educator — organist, harpsichordist, collaborative pianist, choral and orchestral conductor, composer, and writer. A dedicated liturgical musician, he serves as Director of Music and Liturgy and Organist at Holy Family Catholic Church in Glendale, California, where he has built a comprehensive music program: the St. Cecilia Chorale, the Cantus Handbell Ensemble, the Cherubim and Seraphim children's choirs, the Archangels Youth Chorus, and a chamber ensemble.

He is University Organist and a member of the piano faculty at California Lutheran University, where he mentors a studio of young organists and directs a recital series featuring international artists, including the monthly Afternoon Bach Recital Series. He also teaches music theory at the Colburn School in Los Angeles and performs as harpsichordist with Hortus Musicus, an early music consort.

As artistic director and founder of the Glendale Youth Symphony — a nonprofit supported by the Colburn Foundation — he leads young musicians in his community. His choral music is published by MusicSpoke and GIA Publications, with a focus on Latin American and indigenous composers. He holds a Doctor of Musical Arts in sacred music from the University of Southern California, a Master of Arts in organ performance from Claremont Graduate University, and a Bachelor of Music in piano performance from Azusa Pacific University.
